Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business

  1
 session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, and, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other
such times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person
participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-

  3
 hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

   OVERVIEW

The City of South  Gate ("City")  2015 Zoning  Code  prohibits  new industrial  warehouse  development  over 15,000  SF.
Because of the City's  prime  location  near Port  of LA and Long Beach and the growth  of e-commerce,  the City's
industrial  land is in high demand,  Landowners  and developers  are looking  for opportunities  to site new warehouses  and
distribution  centers  in the City.  City  has a number  of industrial  zoned  parcels that  are suited for redevelopment,  but
there  are  questions  as to what  will be acceptable  uses  for this land in the future.

Currently  there  are industrial  parcels in the City that are blighted  and underutilized.  Landowners  and businesses  are
interested  in bringing  in industrial  land uses that  include  warehouse  operations,  as a way to renew  their  parcels.
Industrial  development  with  warehouses  can create  opportunities  for landowners  and create jobs, but they can also
create  negative  impacts  for the community.

The City  Council  directed  staff to review  options  for development  alternatives,  which  are discussed  in this report,
Thus, Kosmont  Companies  ("Kosmont")  was retained  by the City to research  various  policies  adopted  by select cities,
While  there  are a few cities that prohibit  new warehouses,  most create  policies  to generate  substantial  revenue  from
new warehouses,  to offset  traffic  and other  impacts,  and help achieve a better  balance for both the business and
residential  communities.

   OVERVIEW

The scope  of this  Study  and discussion  is to review  alternatives  to the current  restrictions  in place for industrial  use,
including  a 15,000  sq. ft. cap on new warehouse  space. A review  of what  other  cities  do to regulate  industrial  uses is
presented  herein  and the Study  includes:

  Identification  of industrial  areas within  City  of South  Gate  and how truck  trips  are routed
  Review  of three  ways cities  look  to collect  revenue  to offset  impacts  of industrial  uses
  Case studies  of California  cities  industrial  use policies
  Possible  policy  suggestion  for discussion
  Possible  next  steps

It is important  to note  that  the number  one issue concerning  South  Gate  residents  is increased  truck  traffic.  The City
has a limited  number  of truck  routes  that  are focused  at pinch  points  along  Firestone  at Atlantic  Ave, 1-710 freeway  and
Garfield  Aye. as shown  on the following  slide.  It will  be important  for  City  retain  a traffic  expert  to determine  realistic
traffic  volumes  from  a range of warehouse  uses, identify  mitigation  measures  and likely  costs  in order  to calculate  the
development  impact  fees needed  to cover  necessary  roadway  and other  improvements.

The  Kosmont  study,  along with  a focused  traffic  analysis,  will  help the  City  evaluate  potential  changes  to the Zoning
Code  and other  policy  options.

 Land use permission  tables in Section  11.21.030  of the Zoning  Code establish  the uses to which  land in each zone may be put.  Table
  11.21-3 specifies uses allowed in the Urban Mixed-Use  zones, and Table "11.21-4 specifies  uses allowed  in the Commercial  Industrial
  zones.  Under  those tables, warehousing  is permitted  (subject  to issuance by the City of a Conditional  Use Permit)  in the Industrial
  Flex (IF), Light Industrial  (LF), Light Manufacturing  (M2) and Heavy Manufacturing  (M3) zones.  However,  footnote  18 in Table 11.2'l-
  3 and Footnote  Il  in Table I 1.21-4  each limits the size and placement  of warehouses  within  those zones  as follows:

 "Limited  to maximum  building  area  of fifteen  thousand  square  feet  and  is not  permitted  along  street  frontage
  (would  have to be a rear use)."

 These footnotes  were  incorporated  into the South Gate Municipal  Code  in 2015 when  the Planning Commission  prepared,  and the
  Council  enacted,  a comprehensive  update to the Zoning  Code.  The Planning Commissioners  and City Council  Members  who were
  in office  at that time felt the inclusion  of these footnotes  was necessary  to prevent  a proliferation  of large warehouses  in the City
  which  would  cause detrimental  impacts  to the community.

a  While  many cities  have Development  Impact  Fees ("DIF")  that  are charged  to new  industrial  development,  state  law
  requires  nexus  studies  to create  a schedule  of fees by land use type  to assure  parties  are charged  for fair share  of
  infrastructure  costs.  The  standards  used to measure  traffic  impacts  from  new development  are typically  based on
  ITE standards  using the number of employees  at a location, which is -1 per 1,000 SF and fees range from $2 to $5
  per SF. Therefore,  many  Nexus  studies  do  not  necessarily  factor  in the  number  of trips  and  the  time
  of day  involving  warehouse/e-commerce  truck  unloading  and  loading  of goods  for  local  delivery.

s  Kosmont  research  found  that  most  cities  utilize  a Conditional  Use Permit  ("CUP")  or Development  Agreement
  DA")  negotiation  with  industrial  developers  to give the City  flexibility  to negotiate  large impact  fees and annual
  special  taxes  to address  the unique  circumstances  involved  with  wide  range of businesses  utilizing  warehouse  space.
  Our  Study  found  most  concern  with  large scale e-commerce  distribution  facilities,  but many corporations  utilize
  facilities  that  combine  regional  HQ's,  R&D,  manufacturing  and local  Business  to Business  ("B to B") distribution,  that
  vide  high paying jobs,  significant  assessed  value for  property  taxes  and local sales tax generation.

   MUNICIPAL  INDUSTRIAL  POLICY  REFERENCES

A number  of California  municipalities  have enacted  industrial  policies  in recent  years to address  the  influx  of large
distribution  centers  and warehouses  associated  with  the online  retail  industry.  There  is a significant  need for  large
warehouse  facilities  where  sorting,  storage  and ultimate  distribution  of retail  products  can take  place. Concerns  around
these  uses relate  to their  high generation  of truck  trips  paired  with  low job counts  at relatively  low  pay.

   FONTANA

The City of Fontana  has approved  over 16 million  SF of warehouses  in past few years.  The upfront  development  fee
the City charged to cover circulation impacts was approximately  $5,00 per SF of building  area for industrial  uses.  No
fee for municipal  services

Fontana was sued by environmental  groups  over approval  of two  large warehouse  projects  in the southern  part  of the
City.  In 2022 the Attorney  General  of CA announced  a settlement  with  the City that  protects  community  from
pollution.  The City  has adopted  a new ordinance  that  is the strictest  in the State requiring  landscape  buffers,  use  of
solar power,  zero-emission  vehicles,  truck  routing  plans, and prohibition  of off-site  parking  and vehicle  stacking.

   VERNON

In June 2022, pursuant to Government Code Section 65858,the City Council adopted Ordinance No, 1283 (Attachment
2), a 45-day  urgency  moratorium  ordinance.  Ordinance  No. 1283 was adopted  to protect  the public  health,  safety, and
welfare  by prohibiting  the establishment,  expansion,  or modification  of warehouse  uses, freight  terminals,  truck  terminals,
container  storage,  and container  parking  in the City.

Vernon  subsequently  adopted  a permanent  ordinance  (Municipal  Code  Section  17.84.060)  that  requires  new warehouse
in excess  of 150,000  SF must  utilize  a DevelopmentAgreement,  public  hearing  and approval  by the City  Council.

There  has been one project  approved through the DA process.  In March 2024, GPTVernon,  owner  of an old industrial
building  on  7. I acre site at 5764 Alcoa received approval  to demolish  existing  buildings  and construct  a new  153,000 SF
warehouse building.  The DA requires owner to pay $1 million community  benefit fee payable in four installments of
$250,000 each, with a potential credit against year 2 thru year 4 payments for utility taxes paid in excess of a formula
provided in DA. This community  benefit is equal to approximately  $7 per SF for a similar development  proposed in
South  Gate.

   BURBANK

In 2022  the City  of Burbank  commissioned  a Nexus  Study  by EPS and Fehr  Peers to update  the  Development  Impact
Fee ("DIF")  program.  The  Study  analyzed  impact  of expected  new residential,  commercial  and industrial  development
on the  need for  police,  fire, library  and park facilities,  information  technology  and transportation  infrastructure.

For transportation  impact  fees the study  examined  the  increase  in PM peak hour  trips  and estimated  the average  capital
cost to mitigate  be -$10,500 per trip. For warehouse/industrial
  to  the Study used ITE trip generation tables of 0.34PM
